newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger following jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger following jobs data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in heavy trade on Friday, pulled higher by U.S. treasuries, after a volatile session prompted by the release of U.S. and Canadian employment data, analysts said.

"It's led by the U.S. The U.S. had an amazing turnaround this morning," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed income research with Midland Walwyn Capital. "The market was a little bit ahead of itself. There were a lot of shorts out there."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 rose C$0.65 to C$100.70 to yield 7.935 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 16/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
The spread between benchmark bonds narrowed to 83 basis points from 84 basis points at Thursday close.
Canadian and U.S. bond markets see-sawed this morning after the release of a report showing U.S. non-farm payrolls rose a stronger than expected 250,000. Payrolls were expected to rise by 244,000.

For many investors, the report confirmed expectations the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise U.S. interest rates as early as this month. At the same time, the report was not strong enough to make a 50-basis point hike in U.S. interest rates likely, analysts said.

Both Canadian and U.S. bonds sold off early in the session after the release of the data, but later erased early losses to rally by midday amid short-covering. Foreign central bank buying aided gains in U.S. bonds, analysts said.

In Canadian economic news, Statistics Canada today reported employment in Canada grew by a stronger-than-expected 82,000 in August, bringing the unemployment rate for August down to 9.4 percent from 9.8 percent in July.
The signals of Canadian job growth eliminated any remaining expectations in the Canadian market for another Bank of Canada rate cut, said Midland's Dong.
As a result, short-term Canadian bond prices remained under pressure for much of the session.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.45 to C$96.55 to yield 7.487 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 14/32 to yield 6.92 percent.
The spread between the two bonds was 57 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Thursday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 4.02 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.33 percent.
